$comment: A Kotlin value in a tag of an HTML string, judged by both editors alike: in an end tag, which takes no attributes, and `<$name`, which is a tag only when what follows the value could go on one.

cases.name: a %s in an end tag is not told to quote
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(q: String) = interpolate("

x

", q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in an end tag, which takes no attributes, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Write the end tag from literals alone.

cases.name: a template in an end tag is said to be in one

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into an end tag, which takes no attributes: the browser drops them, and a value from outside can still end the tag and write markup. Write the end tag from literals alone.

cases.name: an unquoted template in an end tag is not told to quote

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into an end tag, which takes no attributes: the browser drops them, and a value from outside can still end the tag and write markup. Write the end tag from literals alone.

cases.name: a template in an end tag's name is the structure

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into the markup's own structure: a tag name, an attribute name or a list of attributes. Fine for one chosen in code; a value from outside decides the markup itself, and escaping cannot prevent that.

cases.name: <$name before a backslash is a search pattern, not a tag
cases.source: fun f(tagg: String, html: String) = Regex("<$tagg\\b[^>]*").find(html)

cases.name: <$name at the end of a literal is a search pattern, not a tag
cases.source: fun f(tagg: String, html: String) = html.indexOf("<$tagg")

cases.name: <${name} before another character is not a tag
cases.source: fun f(tagg: String, html: String) = html.indexOf("<${tagg}-x")

cases.name: <$name before a space is a tag
